nodes.name: Rare-earth-doped MnCo2O4.5 synthesis
nodes.procedure: The rare-earth-doped MnCo2O4.5 catalysts (M = Sm, Nd, Ho) were synthesized via ethanol-assisted ultrasonic dispersion of precursor solutions, in situ spray deposition onto Pt/Ti felt substrate, and subsequent pyrolysis at optimized calcination temperature of 250°C (optimized for 10% Sm doping sample). Detailed synthesis procedures including precursor preparation are provided in the Supporting Information.

unit_operations.name: Spray deposition
unit_operations.procedure_snippet: in situ spray deposition onto a Pt/Ti felt

nodes.source_text: Synthesis and Structural Characterization. The rare-earth-doped MnCo2O4.5 catalysts were synthesized via ethanol-assisted ultrasonic dispersion, in situ spray deposition onto a Pt/Ti felt, and subsequent pyrolysis... By optimizing the rare-earth doping calcination temperature and concentration, we determined that the sample calcined at 250°C with 10% Sm doping exhibits the highest electrocatalytic activity (Figures S19 and S20).

The optimized Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ catalyst delivers a remarkably low overpotential of 212 mV at a current density of 10 mA cm⁻² (80% iR compensation)... Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ exhibits the smallest Tafel slope of 38.57 mV dec⁻¹ (Figure 3b), the lowest charge-transfer resistance as revealed by electrochemical impedance spectroscopy (EIS) (Figure S23)... Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ catalyst exhibits excellent chronoamperometric stability at 10 mA cm⁻² with 1200 h (Figure 3d)
as well as Nd- and Ho-doped analogues (234 and 250 mV, respectively)
as well as Nd- and Ho-doped analogues (234 and 250 mV, respectively)
The single-cell exhibits a low cell voltage of 1.73 V at 0.5 A cm⁻² and maintains stable operation over 300 hours

nodes.characterization_summary: All diffraction patterns exhibit characteristic reflections corresponding to the spinel phase of MnCo₂O₄.₅ (PDF#32-0297), with prominent peaks of rare-earth-doped samples shifting toward lower 2θ angles indicating lattice expansion.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The crystalline structures of the resulting M-MnCo₂O₄.₅ samples were investigated via X-ray diffraction (XRD, Figure 1b). All diffraction patterns exhibit characteristic reflections corresponding to the spinel phase of MnCo₂O₄.₅ (PDF#32-0297) ... indicating lattice expansion (Figures S1 and S2).

nodes.characterization_summary: SEM images reveal Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ uniformly covered the Pt/Ti felt, forming a densely interwoven nanoparticle network.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Scanning electron microscopy (SEM) images reveal that the as-obtained Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ uniformly covered the Pt/Ti felt, forming a densely interwoven nanoparticle network ... (Figure 1c and inset).

nodes.characterization_summary: AC-HAADF-STEM shows isolated bright spots corresponding to single Sm atoms in Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ with local lattice strain confirmed by line intensity profiles and GPA maps showing shear and axial strains up to ±1.4%.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Aberration-corrected high-angle annular dark-field scanning transmission electron microscopy (AC-HAADF-STEM) provided direct atomic-scale evidence ... with amplitudes up to ±1.4%. (Figure 1d-f)

nodes.characterization_summary: Elemental composition determined by ICP-MS closely matches nominal ratios of Co, Mn, and rare-earth elements.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The elemental composition of other samples was also determined by both EDS (Figures S7-S9) and inductively coupled plasma-mass spectrometry (ICP-MS, Table S1), and closely matches the nominal ratios.

nodes.characterization_summary: Co 2p spectra show Co²⁺/Co³⁺ peaks at 780.33/795.43 eV for MnCo₂O₄.₅ and 780.62/795.72 eV for Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ with Co³⁺/Co²⁺ ratio increasing from 1.7 to 1.9; Mn 2p shows Mn³⁺/Mn⁴⁺ ratio increasing from 1.1 to 1.2; O 1s shows increased oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co 2p spectra exhibit well-defined Co 2p₃/₂ and Co 2p₁/₂ peaks at approximately 780.33/795.43 eV for MnCo₂O₄.₅ and 780.62/795.72 eV for Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ ... which corresponds to oxygen vacancies. (Figure 2a-c, S10)

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge XANES shows edge shift toward higher energies (0.3 eV) for Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ relative to MnCo₂O₄.₅, indicating increased Co oxidation state.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The Co K-edge X-ray absorption near-edge structure (XANES) spectra of Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ exhibit a noticeable edge shift toward higher energies (0.3 eV) relative to the undoped counterpart ... (Figure 2d).

nodes.characterization_summary: Normalized Co XES shows integrated absolute difference corresponding to 3d spin moment (S_N) decreased from 0.45 to 0.16, indicating substantial reduction in Co spin moment.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The integrated absolute difference (IAD) corresponding to a nominal 3d spin moment (S_N) decreased from 0.45 to 0.16 (Table S2), indicating a substantial reduction in Co spin moment upon Sm doping. (Figure 2e)

nodes.characterization_summary: Temperature-dependent EPR spectra show Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ with intermediate g ≈ 2.05, nonmonotonic ΔB_pp near 150 K indicating spin-state transition; stronger g = 2.003 signal confirms oxygen vacancies.
nodes.evidence_snippet: Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ displays an intermediate g value and a nonmonotonic peak-to-peak line width (ΔB_pp) near 150 K ... The Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ sample exhibits a significantly stronger signal at g = 2.003, which is attributed to unpaired electrons associated with surface defects, primarily oxygen vacancies (Figure S11).

nodes.characterization_summary: Room-temperature magnetic susceptibility χ of Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ is 1.96 × 10⁻⁵ emu g⁻¹ vs 4.62 × 10⁻⁵ emu g⁻¹ for MnCo₂O₄.₅; effective magnetic moment decreases from 6.70 μ_B to 4.60 μ_B.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The room-temperature magnetic susceptibility (χ) of Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ is significantly lower (1.96 × 10⁻⁵ emu g⁻¹) than that of MnCo₂O₄.₅ (4.62 × 10⁻⁵ emu g⁻¹) ... After Sm incorporation, the effective magnetic moments (μ_eff) drastically decrease to 4.60 μ_B. (Figure 2g,h, S18, Table S3)

nodes.characterization_summary: In-situ XANES shows Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ with minor edge shift (0.23 eV) vs pronounced shift (1.25 eV) for MnCo₂O₄.₅ under OER potentials, indicating restricted Co oxidation.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In-situ XANES analysis reveals that pristine MnCo₂O₄.₅ undergoes a pronounced edge shift (1.25 eV) ... whereas Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ shows only a minor edge shift (0.23 eV) ... (Figure 4a,b).

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Raman shows characteristic spinel modes E_g, F_{2g}, A_{1g} (≈480-700 cm⁻¹) remain discernible for Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ across OER potential range with minor shifts.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ Raman spectroscopy ... the characteristic spinel modes E_g, F_{2g}, and A_{1g} (≈480-700 cm⁻¹) remain discernible across the entire potential range ... (Figure 4g).

nodes.characterization_summary: Co K-edge EXAFS shows Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ first-shell Co-O peak shifts to shorter distance (~1.5 Å) with broadening; second-shell splits into Co_oct-M_oct and Co_tet-M_oct configurations.
nodes.evidence_snippet: The R-space extended X-ray absorption fine structure (EXAFS) analysis (Figure S12b) further reveals that Sm doping perturbs the local metal-oxygen coordination environment ... reflecting a significant rearrangement in the Co coordination geometry.

nodes.characterization_summary: In situ Co K-edge EXAFS shows Sm-MnCo₂O₄.₅ maintains sharp Co-O peaks with minor reversible bond contractions during OER, while MnCo₂O₄.₅ shows strong attenuation and continuous contraction.
nodes.evidence_snippet: In situ EXAFS analysis further reveals pronounced structural differences ... with only minor and reversible bond contractions, while the Co-Mn features remain clearly resolved (Figure 4d,e).
